papers.title: Neural Surrogates for Tabulated Nuclear Equations of State in Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations
papers.result: Along isentropes at $Y_e=0.3$, maximum relative errors reach $6.6\%$, $14.2\%$, and $29.7\%$ for $P$, $c_s$, and $\Gamma$. Additional shock tubes keep relative $L_1$ errors below $2.5\times 10^{-3}$ in $\rho$ and $P$ and below $4.5\times 10^{-3}$ in $v$, with fiducial hydrodynamic errors $\sim 10^{-3}$. A $64\times 4$ network stores $\sim 100\,\mathrm{kB}$ versus $\sim 160\,\mathrm{MB}$ for LS220 ($\sim 1500\times$); lower validation MSE does not necessarily reduce hydrodynamic error.
papers.problem: Tabulated nuclear EOSs make memory a practical constraint in massively parallel core-collapse simulations, and pointwise thermodynamic accuracy does not by itself determine hydrodynamic fidelity.
papers.method: A network maps $(\log_{10}\rho,\log_{10}e,Y_e)$ to $P$, $\Gamma$, and $c_s$ with $\mathcal{L}=w_P\mathcal{L}_P+w_\Gamma\mathcal{L}_\Gamma+w_{c_s}\mathcal{L}_{c_s}$ and baseline weights $(10,1,8)$. Tests are Godunov shock tubes, truncated TOV equilibria $$\frac{dP}{dr}=-\frac{G(\epsilon+P)(m+4\pi r^{3}P/c^{2})}{c^{2}r^{2}(1-2Gm/rc^{2})},\qquad \frac{dm}{dr}=\frac{4\pi r^{2}\epsilon}{c^{2}},$$ with $\epsilon=\rho(c^{2}+e)$, and a 1D adiabatic collapse.
papers.reason: This is a memory-reduction neural surrogate for tabulated nuclear EOS calls in CCSN hydrodynamics, not a result on central engines, neutrinos, shock breakout, jets, FRBs, or compact-object high-energy observables.

papers.title: Noise and quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole accretion flows
papers.result: QPOs occur only in geometrically thick advection-dominated accretion flows and are absent in geometrically thin cooling-dominated flows. Thick-flow accretion-rate fluctuations obey a telegraph-type equation; for uncorrelated viscosity fluctuations with radial index $b$, $P(\omega)\propto\omega^{-1-4b/3}(1-\omega^{1/3})^{2}\left|\tilde{Q}_{\rm out}(\omega^{-1/3},\omega)/\tilde{Q}_{\rm out}(1,\omega)\right|^{2}$ over $X_{\rm out}^{-3}<\omega<1$. Outer-radius reflection is required to generate the QPO. Cooling-dominated disks instead give $P(\omega)\propto\omega^{-1-10b/7}$.

papers.title: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
papers.result: Most standard SNe II are consistent with low-density circumstellar medium (CSM) environments characterized by mass-loss rate $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$, wind velocity $v_w \approx 50\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, and standard explosion kinetic energy $E_k = (0.6\text{--}1.2)\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$. Discrepancies in early UV continuum brightness indicate progenitor initial radii larger than standard models ($R_* > 500\ \mathrm{R_\odot}$). In contrast, SNe with confined dense CSM require substantially enhanced mass-loss rates, such as SN 2024faq with $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ ($R_{\rm CSM} \approx 2\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$) and SN 2023ixf with $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ ($R_{\rm CSM} \approx 6\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$, $E_k \approx 1.2\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$). Narrow C III $\lambda 2297$ emission traces persistent photoionization at $r > 8\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$ ahead of a shock moving at $v_{\rm shock} \approx 10^4\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ with unshocked wind velocity $v_{\rm wind} \approx 25\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$. In addition, UV resonance line transitions have large optical depths ($\tau_{\rm line} \gg 1$) undergoing repeated line-scattering, rendering UV emission intrinsically directional and sensitive to multi-dimensional CSM asymmetry.
papers.problem: The physical origins of early-time ultraviolet diversity and spectral heterogeneity across young core-collapse supernovae, specifically resolving whether early UV flux and line profiles are governed by RSG progenitor envelope structures, shock cooling, or confined dense circumstellar material (CSM) interaction and geometric asymmetry.
papers.method: Target of Opportunity (ToO) UV spectroscopy from HST/STIS (G230LB, G430L, G750L spanning $\sim 1600\text{--}10000\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) within $\delta t \lesssim 2\ \mathrm{weeks}$ of first light, combined with Swift/UVOT and ZTF multiband photometry, host extinction correction via Na I D equivalent width $A_V^{\rm host} = (0.78 \pm 0.15)\ \mathrm{mag} \times ({\rm EW}_{\rm NaID}/\mathrm{\mathring{A}})$, and 1D non-LTE radiative transfer modeling using CMFGEN across varying mass-loss rates $\dot{M} = 10^{-6}\text{--}10^{-1}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ and explosion energies $E_k = (0.6\text{--}1.2)\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$.
papers.reason: This work presents the largest early-time ($\delta t \lesssim 2\ \mathrm{weeks}$) HST UV spectroscopic sample of young core-collapse supernovae to date, establishing decisive constraints on shock breakout cooling, progenitor radii, and circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction.

papers.title: Super-Eddington Accretion onto Compact Objects: Theory Meets Observation
papers.result: Super-Eddington accretion breaks the spherical limit, yielding logarithmic total disk luminosity scaling $L/L_{\rm Edd} \approx 1 + \ln(\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm Edd})$ due to radial photon advection within the photon trapping radius $R_{\rm tr} = (\dot{M}c^2/L_{\rm Edd})r_g$, with maximum effective temperature $T_{\rm eff,max} \simeq 0.2(M_{\rm BH}/10^5 M_\odot)^{-1/4}\ {\rm keV}$. Radiative efficiency decreases monotonically with accretion rate from $\sim 5.4\%$ down to $0.45\%$ at $\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm Edd} \approx 149$ for radiation-pressure disks, while magnetically arrested disks (MAD) drive relativistic jets and ultrafast outflows ($v \sim 0.1-0.3c$) with kinetic power reaching $\sim 0.1\%-5\% L_{\rm bol}$, and bulk Comptonization naturally produces the soft X-ray excess.
papers.problem: Reconciling multi-wavelength observational peculiarities of super-Eddington systems—such as suppressed UV/optical variability, soft X-ray excess, weak hard X-ray emission, reverberation mapping lag deficits, and moderate beaming inferred from ULX nebulae—with theoretical radiation MHD accretion disk and outflow models.
papers.method: Multi-dimensional radiation magnetohydrodynamic (radiation MHD) simulations (comparing M1 closure and angle-resolved radiative transfer, SANE vs. MAD regimes) combined with semi-analytic slim disk models, reverberation mapping, and multi-band bolometric correction scaling (e.g. $L_{\rm bol} = 9.26 L_{5100}$ or $5.4 L_{5100}$).
papers.reason: This review comprehensively synthesizes observational properties and multi-dimensional radiation MHD simulations of super-Eddington accretion across stellar-mass to supermassive black holes, directly addressing high-energy accretion dynamics, relativistic outflows, and early black hole growth.

papers.title: The Lives and Deaths of Red Supergiants
papers.result: RSG steady-wind mass-loss rates are constrained to $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-6}\text{--}10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ (insufficient for single-star wind envelope stripping), while flash spectroscopy and early shock-breakout light curves require short-lived pre-explosion rates of $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-4}\text{--}10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ producing confined CSM with $M_{\rm CSM} \lesssim 0.1\,M_\odot$. In SN 2023ixf, extensive envelope stripping ($M_{\rm env} \lesssim 3\,M_\odot$ for $M_{\rm init} \gtrsim 17\,M_\odot$) is decoupled from final pre-explosion dense CSM ejection, while the Red Supergiant Problem is largely reconciled by near-IR bolometric corrections ($\Delta \mathrm{BC} \sim 2.8\,\mathrm{mag}$, shifting luminosities by $1.1\pm 0.5\,\mathrm{dex}$).
papers.problem: Empirical RSG mass-loss prescriptions in stellar evolution codes overpredict total shed mass by up to a factor of 30, and the apparent absence of high-luminosity progenitors for Type II-P supernovae (the Red Supergiant Problem) conflicts with standard core-collapse predictions.
papers.method: Multi-wavelength synthesis combining mid-infrared SED dust radiative transfer models, ALMA millimeter CO rotational transition dynamics, hydrodynamic wind models (comparing radiatively driven wind models against fixed-velocity models), coeval star-cluster calibrations, and pre-explosion photometric SED reconstruction.
papers.reason: This review comprehensively synthesizes RSG mass-loss rates, the Humphreys-Davidson limit, Type II-P plateau mechanics, and pre-supernova circumstellar medium interaction critical for transient modeling.

papers.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $γ$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.result: For transient sources (burst duration $\Delta T = 10^7\,\mathrm{s}$) in $B_{\mathrm{void}} = 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{G}$, magnetic time delay $\Delta t_B$ strongly suppresses counterparts below tens of $\mathrm{GeV}$. Fermi-LAT sensitivity in $1\text{--}10\,\mathrm{TeV}$ shows a nearly flat or slightly decreasing threshold flux with distance due to cascade accumulation compensating cosmological dimming, whereas VHE observatories (HAWC and LHAASO) experience steep threshold increases beyond $z \gtrsim 0.2$ driven by EBL absorption and the $E_{\gamma}\varepsilon(1-\mu) \gtrsim 2m_e^2 c^4$ threshold.

papers.title: A search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst in the M81 globular cluster, FRB 20200120E
papers.result: Detected a single radio burst from FRB 20200120E with $\mathrm{FWHM} = 79.2 \pm 3.5\,\mu\mathrm{s}$, radio fluence $\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} = 0.14 \pm 0.01\,\mathrm{Jy\,ms}$, and equivalent isotropic radio energy $E_{\rm R} = 1.4 \times 10^{33}\,\mathrm{erg}$ via $E_{\rm R} = 9.5 \times 10^{31} \left(\frac{4\pi}{1+z}\right) \left(\frac{d_{\rm L}}{\mathrm{Mpc}}\right)^2 \left(\frac{\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} \cdot \Delta\nu}{\mathrm{Jy\,ms\cdot GHz}}\right)\,\mathrm{erg}$ at $d_{\rm L} = 3.63\,\mathrm{Mpc}$. papers.problem: Investigates whether repeating fast radio bursts produce prompt, millisecond-duration optical counterparts, testing theoretical predictions such as synchrotron maser emission in relativistic shocks or inverse-Compton scattering in magnetar environments.
papers.method: Conducted simultaneous 5-band ($u_s g_s r_s i_s z_s$) high-speed optical photometry using HiPERCAM on the 10.4 m GTC in drift mode (11.98 ms exposure, 1.66 ms dead time, 0.1 ms GPS accuracy) alongside 1.3–6 GHz radio monitoring with the Effelsberg 100 m telescope (coherent dedispersion at $\mathrm{DM} = 87.7527\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$), applying aperture photometry, multi-scale binning, and Lomb-Scargle periodicity searches.
papers.reason: Provides the deepest simultaneous high-speed optical limit to date for the nearby repeating FRB 20200120E in M81, establishing an optical-to-radio fluence ratio limit of $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O}/\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} < 0.013$.

papers.title: Theoretical Instability Models of Quasi-Periodic Eruptions
papers.result: Assesses dynamical and thermal-viscous disk instability models: differential Lense–Thirring precession produces disk tearing on nodal precession timescales $\tau_{\rm np} = \frac{1}{2a}\left(\frac{R}{R_g}\right)^3\left(\frac{GM}{c^3}\right)$ matching observed periods $t_{\rm rec} \sim 2\text{--}50\text{ h}$, whereas standard radiation pressure instability (RPI) viscous timescales $t_{\rm visc} \sim \alpha^{-1}\left(\frac{H}{R}\right)^{-2}\Omega_{\rm K}^{-1}$ are orders of magnitude too long unless the disk is severely truncated ($R_{\rm out} \lesssim 15 R_{\rm Schw}$) or stabilized by modified stress $\tau_{r\phi} = \alpha P_{\rm gas}^\mu P_{\rm tot}^{1-\mu}$ and magnetic cooling.
papers.problem: Investigates whether quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) in repeating extranuclear transients originate from intrinsic accretion disk instabilities (dynamical tearing or radiation-pressure thermal-viscous limit cycles) versus extrinsic orbital or geometrical impact scenarios.
papers.method: One-dimensional time-dependent accretion disk simulations (GLADIS) and limit-cycle analysis solving entropy balance $\Sigma T \frac{\partial S}{\partial t} = Q^+ - Q^-$ and surface density diffusion $\frac{\partial \Sigma}{\partial t} = C_{\rm thv} k(T, \Sigma)$ with wind mass loss $f_{\rm out} = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + A \dot{m}^2}$, evaluating tearing criteria under bending-wave ($\alpha \lesssim H/R$) and diffusive ($\alpha \gtrsim H/R$) regimes.
papers.reason: This review evaluates theoretical accretion disk instability models for quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs), providing valuable physics-based constraints on emission mechanisms, timescales, and disk geometry relevant to high-energy compact object astrophysics.

papers.title: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
papers.result: Resolved a persistent double-lobed non-thermal radio source $\mathrm{GMRT_{ext}}$ with spectral indices between Band 3 (300--500 MHz) and Band 5 (1060--1460 MHz) of $\alpha = -0.3$ (north lobe A), $-0.4$ (south lobe B), and $-0.26$ (core C), corresponding to electron energy indices $p = 1.6$, $1.8$, and $1.52$. Band 4 flux exhibits a $3.06\sigma$--$4.4\sigma$ deviation indicating multi-year variability and source scale $\lesssim 1\text{ pc}$. Jet-to-counterjet flux ratio yields an inclination angle $\theta = 86.57^{\circ} \pm 1.15^{\circ}$ under $\beta\cos\theta = (J^{1/p}-1)/(J^{1/p}+1)$ with relativistic velocity $\beta \sim 1$ and $p = 2+\alpha$. Multiwavelength SED modeling favors a lepto-hadronic scenario for source distance $d = 1.0\text{ kpc}$, radius $R_{sc} = 4.3\text{ pc}$, and magnetic field $B = 1$--$5\,\mu\mathrm{G}$.
papers.problem: Identifying the low-energy counterpart and nature of the dark PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157, which lacks confirmed counterparts and exhibits ambiguous leptonic versus hadronic ultra-high-energy emission mechanisms.
papers.method: Conducted high-resolution continuum observations using uGMRT Band 3 (300--500 MHz, 200 MHz bandwidth) and Band 5 (1060--1460 MHz, 400 MHz bandwidth) calibrated with CASA, followed by spatially resolved spectral index mapping and multi-wavelength SED modeling incorporating leptonic and lepto-hadronic particle distributions with a cutoff power law $\frac{dN}{dE} = N_0 \left(\frac{E}{1\,\mathrm{TeV}}\right)^{\alpha} \exp\left[-\left(\frac{E}{E_{\rm cut}}\right)^{\beta}\right]$.
papers.reason: This paper presents multi-band uGMRT low-frequency radio observations of the dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157, resolving a persistent double-lobed jet structure that constrains microquasar and compact-object cosmic-ray accelerator models.

papers.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.result: The flux eruption initiates at $t = 20040\,t_g$, during which equatorial magnetic reconnection reduces magnetic support and drives an equatorward electromagnetic energy flux $-\langle T^\theta_{{\rm EM}\,t}\rangle_\phi > 0$ that channels energy from off-equatorial latitudes toward the equator. A non-axisymmetric magnetic bubble characterized by low density ($\rho < 3$ and $\rho < 0.3\max_\phi \rho$) and high magnetization $\sigma = b^2/\rho$ expands radially out to $r \approx 6\,r_g$ by $t = 20160\,t_g$, propelled outward by the magnetic-pressure-dominated total pressure gradient $-\sqrt{-g}\,\partial_r p_{\rm tot}$ and outward magnetic tension $\mathcal{F}_{\rm ten} = \partial_j(\sqrt{-g}\,b^j b_r) - \sqrt{-g}\,b^\mu b_\nu \Gamma^\nu_{r\mu} > 0$.
papers.problem: Resolving the spatial dichotomy and dynamical connection in magnetically arrested disks (MADs) where the horizon-threading magnetic flux $\Phi_B$ drops precipitously in off-equatorial regions ($\theta \sim 0.5$--$1.0$ and $\theta \sim 2.2$--$2.8$) while mass accretion $(-\rho u^r)$ and magnetic reconnection occur predominantly along the equatorial plane.
papers.method: 3D GRMHD simulation using Athena++ in Kerr-Schild coordinates around a black hole with spin $a = 0.98$ (MAD98) at resolution $N_r \times N_\theta \times N_\phi = 1408 \times 512 \times 256$, tracking the mass accretion rate $\dot{M} = -\iint \sqrt{-g}\,\rho\,u^r\,d\theta d\phi$, magnetic flux $\Phi_B = \iint \sqrt{-g}\,|B^r|\,d\theta d\phi$, dimensionless flux $\phi_B = \Phi_B / \sqrt{\dot{M}}$, and stress-energy components $T^\mu_{\ \nu}$ with total pressure $p_{\rm tot} = p_{\rm gas} + b^2/2$.
papers.reason: This high-resolution 3D GRMHD study uncovers the physical coupling between magnetic reconnection and magnetic bubble expansion during MAD flux eruptions, offering critical theoretical insights into relativistic jet dynamics and compact object flaring.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.result: In low-luminosity states ($L_{\rm X} \lesssim 10^{35}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$), SFXTs enter the subsonic settling accretion regime where IGR J16418$-$4532 displays a two-hump spectrum with intersection energy $E_{\rm int} = 10.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\,{\rm keV}$ and cyclotron line energy $E_{\rm cyc} = 53.9^{+2.3}_{-1.8}\,{\rm keV}$ yielding $E_{\rm cyc}/E_{\rm int} = 5.1^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$; IGR J17544$-$2619 shows $E_{\rm cyc} \sim 27\,{\rm keV}$ with $E_{\rm int} = 7.3\pm 0.3\,{\rm keV}$ ($E_{\rm cyc}/E_{\rm int} = 3.6\pm 0.2$) and flux ratio $F_{\rm low}/F_{\rm high}$ varying from $0.31\pm 0.01$ to $0.45\pm 0.01$ across states.
papers.problem: Testing whether the characteristic two-hump spectral morphology and empirical scaling relation $E_{\rm cyc} \approx 4.15 E_{\rm int}$ observed in Be/X-ray binaries universally apply to wind-accreting supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) at low accretion rates.
papers.method: Broadband X-ray spectral analysis (0.5–79 keV) combining XMM-Newton, NICER, and NuSTAR observations using XSPEC v12.15.1 with single and double Comptonization models (`comptt` and `comptt+comptt`), Gaussian cyclotron absorption lines (`gabs`), and MCMC parameter estimation.
papers.reason: This paper investigates low-state X-ray accretion regimes and spectral formation in magnetized neutron stars within SFXTs, directly providing observational constraints and spectral models for compact object high-energy astrophysics.

papers.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.result: Measures unabsorbed 3–79 keV luminosities across states from $L_{3-79} \simeq (5.05 \pm 0.01) \times 10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ down to $(5.8^{+0.4}_{-0.3}) \times 10^{34}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Identifies a transition from a cutoff power-law continuum to a two-hump Comptonized spectrum with intersection energy $E_{\rm int} = 11.7^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\ \mathrm{keV}$, yielding $E_{\rm cyc}/E_{\rm int} = 4.5 \pm 0.2$ consistent with the cyclotron resonant scattering feature at $E_{\rm cyc} = 52.1^{+0.5}_{-0.9}\ \mathrm{keV}$ and scaling relation $E_{\rm cyc} = (4.15 \pm 0.11)E_{\rm int}$, implying a neutron star surface magnetic field of $B_{12} = \frac{1+z}{11.6}E_{\rm cyc} \simeq 6$ ($B \sim 6 \times 10^{12}\ \mathrm{G}$).
papers.problem: Investigating whether strongly magnetized accreting pulsars develop a two-hump spectrum at low accretion rates through cyclotron photon thermalization and Comptonization, and determining whether the source enters the propeller regime.
papers.method: Joint spectral fitting of NuSTAR and Swift/XRT observations with HEASoft v6.36 using a two-component thermal Comptonization continuum (`comptt + comptt`) and applying detector bad-pixel masks (`fpma_userbpfile`, `fpmb_userbpfile`) for stray-light filtering.
papers.reason: Investigates the accretion state transition and broadband X-ray spectral evolution in the Be/X-ray binary pulsar IGR J06074+2205, testing theoretical models of two-hump Comptonized spectra at low accretion rates.

papers.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
papers.result: AT 2025abao is an AGB-star common-envelope merger ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, $q \approx 0.10_{-0.05}^{+0.10}$) exhibiting an optical eruption with peak luminosity $L \approx 2.5 \times 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, an $\approx 80\,\mathrm{d}$ plateau, and ejecta-CSM shock interaction with $v_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ decelerating from $\approx 900\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $\approx 150\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ matching $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$. The orbital dissipation energy $\Delta E_{\rm orb} \approx 10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg}$ predominantly drives kinetic ejection ($KE_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg}$ for $M_{\rm ej} \approx 0.1\text{--}0.2\,M_\odot$) rather than binding energy unbinding ($E_{\rm unbind} \approx 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or radiation ($E_{\rm rad} \approx 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg}$), governed by $\Delta E_{\rm orb} = E_{\rm unbind} + E_{\rm rad} + KE_{\rm ej}$.
papers.problem: Direct observational verification of binary common envelope evolution (CEE) dynamics, specifically how orbital energy is dissipated by drag during inspiral and whether envelope unbinding or kinetic ejection dominates the energy sink.
papers.method: Multiband photometric monitoring (ZTF, WINTER, WIRC, Cerberus high-cadence SDSS-$r$ with $1\,\mathrm{s}$ sampling), Swift UVOT/XRT, SPHEREx ($0.7\text{--}5\,\mu\mathrm{m}$), and JWST/MIRI SED modeling. Progenitor quiescent mass loss is modeled via $\dot{M} = \eta_{\rm gd}\frac{4\pi v_{\rm wind}R_{\rm in}\tau_V}{\kappa_V} \sim 10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$, and precursor drag dissipation is quantified by $L_{\rm decay} = 4\pi G^{3/2}C_d M_2^2 \rho a^{1/2}(M_1+M_2)^{-1/2} \propto a^{-5/2} \approx 3\times 10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with MESA envelope binding energy $E_{\rm bind}(>m) = \int_m^{M_\star}\left(-\frac{Gm_r}{r}+u\right)\mathrm{d}m$.
papers.reason: This paper presents the first direct observational identification of common-envelope evolution (CEE) orbital inspiral and merger in M31 (AT 2025abao), directly revealing ejecta-CSM shock interaction and plateau energetics relevant to high-energy transient physics.

papers.title: The Population of Radio Hypernebulae from Mass-Transferring Massive Binaries
papers.result: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$. The systems launch mildly relativistic jets ($v_{\rm j} \sim 0.1\text{--}0.3c$) and disk winds ($v_{\rm w} \sim 0.03c$) inflating long-lived synchrotron hypernebulae with peak radio luminosities $L_{\nu,\rm peak} \sim 10^{28}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{GHz}$, overlapping with FRB-associated PRSs and yielding $\sim 10^{2\text{--}5}$ detectable steady sources in VLASS.
papers.problem: Distinguishing unresolved synchrotron hypernebulae driven by rare, energetic hyper-Eddington binary mass transfer from other populations of unresolved synchrotron sources (such as AGNs, SNRs, and GRB afterglows) in modern wide-field radio surveys.
papers.method: Coupled COMPAS binary population synthesis (v02.35.03) with a semi-analytic synchrotron hypernebula model. For stable RLOF, the mass-transfer rate is set by donor envelope thermal timescale $\dot{M} = \dot{M}_{\rm th} = M_{\rm d,env}/\tau_{\rm KH} = R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}/(G M_{\rm d})$ with duration $t_{\rm acc} = \tau_{\rm KH}$, whereas unstable common-envelope evolution incorporates pre-dynamical accretion $\dot{M} = f_{\rm acc}\Delta M_{\rm CE}/(100 P_{\rm orb})$. Jet kinetic luminosity scales as $L_{\rm j} = \eta L_{\rm w} \simeq \frac{1}{2}\eta \dot{M} v_{\rm w}^2$ with efficiency $\eta \sim 0.1$, injecting relativistic electrons at the termination shock.
papers.reason: This paper presents the first binary population synthesis coupled with time-dependent synchrotron nebular models for hyper-Eddington mass-transfer systems, directly constraining persistent radio source (PRS) counterparts to repeating FRBs, relativistic jet inflation, and radio transient surveys.

papers.title: A Butterfly Collector's View of Fast Radio Bursts: Repeating Sources Go Quiet within a Few Years
papers.result: Steady Poisson repeater activity is excluded at $p < 10^{-4}$, with the predicted-to-observed burst ratio dropping from $R(\Delta \le 60\ \mathrm{days}) \approx 1$ to $R(\Delta = 360\ \mathrm{days}) = 0.57 \pm 0.11$, giving an activity ratio $S = 0.530 \pm 0.142$. Fitting cessation models yields an active lifetime $\tau = 2.9^{+1.1}_{-0.9}\ \mathrm{yr}$ for a single-lifetime model, an on/off model with active duration $T_{\rm on} = 800^{+400}_{-400}\ \mathrm{days}$ and duty cycle $d = 0.3^{+0.05}_{-0.2}$, or a mixture model with short lifetime $\tau_s = 500^{+300}_{-200}\ \mathrm{days}$ and long-lived fraction $\eta = 0.3^{+0.2}_{-0.1}$. For an FRB volumetric rate $\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB} = 7.3 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the required birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1\left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right)\left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right)\left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right)\left(\frac{100\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$.
papers.problem: Whether repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources maintain stationary burst rates indefinitely or cease activity within months to years as predicted by magnetar central engine models.
papers.method: Formulates an unseen-species estimation framework utilizing Robbins formula $n^{\rm pred}_k = (k+1) N_{k+1} \frac{T_B}{T_A}$ across time windows of length $W = 180\ \mathrm{d}$ separated by gap $\Delta$, evaluating the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = \frac{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 n^{\rm obs}_k(s)}{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 t(s)(k+1)N_{k+1}(s)}$ and decay ratio $S = \frac{R(\Delta \geq 360\ \mathrm{d})}{R(\Delta \leq 90\ \mathrm{d})}$, with exposure calibrated via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k \geq 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.
papers.reason: This paper establishes a novel unseen-species statistical framework on CHIME/FRB repeaters, ruling out steady Poisson activity at $p < 10^{-4}$ and demonstrating that repeating FRBs go quiet on a timescale of a few years.

papers.title: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
papers.result: SN 2025wiu displays peak absolute magnitudes of $M_u = -17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_g = -18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_r = -18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, accompanied by early shock cooling from a compact progenitor with $R_\star \approx 4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 2\,M_\odot$, and $E \approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$. At $\sim 50\,\mathrm{days}$ post-maximum, it develops a secondary bump peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with total radiated energy $E_{\mathrm{bump}} \sim 10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and duration $\Delta t \approx 42\,\mathrm{days}$. Synthesized $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ mass estimated from the primary peak via Arnett's rule is $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} \approx 0.47\,M_\odot$, contrasting sharply with late-time radioactive tail deposition ($f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$ with $T_0 = 173^{+44}_{-41}\,\mathrm{days}$) which yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$. The bump energy implies an interacting CSM mass of $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_\odot$ at radius $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether the high peak luminosity and prominent post-maximum bump of the slowly evolving Type Ib supernova SN 2025wiu can be reconciled with standard radioactive decay, or whether delayed circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, magnetar spin-down, fallback accretion, or a double-$^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ distribution is required.
papers.method: Multi-epoch optical and NIR photometry combined with optical spectroscopy, analytical $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ radioactive decay modeling via the Arnett rule and deposition function $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, photon diffusion timescale constraints ($t_{\mathrm{d}} = \sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}} / (4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}} c)}$), shock cooling emission modeling, and semi-analytical decomposed light-curve fitting involving CSM interaction and magnetar spin-down models.
papers.reason: SN 2025wiu provides exceptional multi-band photometric and spectroscopic coverage of an extraordinary Type Ib supernova with a post-maximum bump, providing quantitative constraints on shock cooling, central engine activity, and circumstellar medium interaction.

papers.title: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
papers.result: By scaling the ejecta mass to $M = 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving expansion velocities (with half the mass concentrated at radial velocities $v_{r} \lesssim 0.09c$ and peak density at $0.04c$), the 3D model reproduces the bolometric luminosity and optical-to-NIR spectra of AT2017gfo at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$, $2.4\,\mathrm{d}$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$ across $5500\text{--}15\,000\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. The reduced velocity compresses the ejecta density, raising the $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ and boosting deposited power by $\sim 30\%$ at $1\text{--}4\,\mathrm{d}$. Through the effective temperature scaling $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4}(v_{\mathrm{ph}}t)^{-1/2}$, smaller photospheric radii $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}}t$ maintain higher photospheric temperatures and avoid premature reddening. Key spectroscopic identifications include: $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$ generating the $\sim 10\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ NIR peak; $\mathrm{Y\ II}\ \lambda 7882$ contributing to the $\sim 7300\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ peak; $\mathrm{La\ III}\ \lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\ III}\ \lambda 14333$ forming the $\sim 13\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ shoulder; and $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda 4216$ creating the blue flux cutoff at $\lesssim 4500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models are dimmer by a factor of $\sim 3$ at $\sim 1\,\mathrm{d}$ because azimuthal averaging artificially mixes lanthanide-poor channels ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$) with high-opacity lanthanides.
papers.problem: First-principles numerical relativity simulations yield 3D dynamical ejecta with masses ($M \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and expansion velocities ($v_{\mathrm{max}} \approx 0.48c$) that are too low in mass and too high in speed compared to empirical AT2017gfo inferences ($M \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), causing synthesized light curves to decay prematurely and spectra to peak at overly red or Doppler-shifted wavelengths; furthermore, whether a physically distinct, unmixed lanthanide-poor component is strictly needed to explain the early blue emission remains unresolved.
papers.method: Multi-dimensional time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS applied to a 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) binary neutron star merger model ($2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, SFHo equation of state) mapped at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Bound-bound transitions ($4.9 \times 10^{7}$ transitions across 83 elements, $Z=57\text{--}70$ in AD3) are computed under local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Radiative transfer is evaluated across line-by-line (LBL) Sobolev optical depths $\tau_i$, expansion opacities $\kappa_{\mathrm{exp}} = \frac{1}{ct\rho}\sum_i \frac{\lambda_i}{\Delta\lambda}(1 - e^{-\tau_i})$, and capped line-binned opacities with optical depth threshold $\tau_{\mathrm{l,max}}$ where bin optical depth is $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and transmission probability $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}}$.
papers.reason: This work presents 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer simulations of the kilonova AT2017gfo, demonstrating that mass scaling and velocity compression of dynamical ejecta self-consistently reproduce the bolometric light curve and early multi-epoch spectra without requiring an ad hoc separate lanthanide-poor component.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of SAX J1808.4-3658's Very Bright Thermonuclear X-ray Burst on the Accretion Disc with NICER
papers.result: Using NICER observations of the PRE thermonuclear burst, Model C simultaneously models reflection and persistent emission evolution, finding an enhanced persistent factor $f_{a,1} = 59.6 \pm 0.6$ and reflection fraction $f_{r,1} = 0.82 \pm 0.15$ with a sub-Eddington peak bolometric luminosity of $L_{\mathrm{burst,1}} \approx 0.68\,L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$. The disc ionization parameter drops from $\log \xi = 3.44^{+0.06}_{-0.17}$ at the first peak to $3.09^{+0.19}_{-0.14}$ at the second peak, while the burst blackbody temperature evolves from $kT_{\mathrm{burst}} = 2.25 \pm 0.05\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($R_{\mathrm{burst}} = 8.51 \pm 2.44\,\mathrm{km}$) to $2.15^{+0.07}_{-0.06}\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($R_{\mathrm{burst}} = 7.66 \pm 2.22\,\mathrm{km}$). In the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$), column density increases by $\approx 34\%\text{--}46\%$ ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (2.42^{+0.13}_{-0.10}) \times 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$) and the disc blackbody temperature increases by $\approx 15\%$, confirming geometric disc puffing that obscures the neutron star surface.
papers.problem: The physical origin of the prominent soft excess ($<1.5\,\mathrm{keV}$) and apparent sub-Eddington peak luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 0.68\,L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$) during a photospheric radius expansion (PRE) Type-I thermonuclear burst, distinguishing between variable accretion disc blackbody emission, relativistic disc reflection, and an evolving persistent accretion component.
papers.method: Time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy was carried out in the $0.5\text{--}10\,\mathrm{keV}$ energy range using Xspec v.12.13.1. Three spectral models were evaluated: Model A with variable disc blackbody ($\mathrm{tbabs} \times (\mathrm{bbodyrad} + \mathrm{diskbb} + \mathrm{nthcomp} + \mathrm{gauss})$); Model B with relativistic reflection ($\mathrm{tbabs} \times (\mathrm{bbodyrad} + (\mathrm{rdblur} \times \mathrm{bbrefl}) + \mathrm{gauss} + \mathrm{diskbb} + \mathrm{nthcomp})$) with tied iron abundance $A_{\mathrm{Fe}} = 2.09 \pm 0.05$; and Model C combining Model B with the $f_a$-method by scaling persistent emission parameters with a constant $f_a$ alongside reflection fraction $f_r = F_{\mathrm{bbrefl}} / F_{\mathrm{bbodyrad}}$.
papers.reason: This paper presents the first simultaneous detection and decoupling of relativistic disc reflection and an evolving persistent accretion component during a bright thermonuclear X-ray burst in SAX J1808.4-3658, providing compelling spectroscopic evidence for burst-induced accretion disc puffing.

papers.title: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
papers.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively. In the intrinsic population, $\sim 94\%$ of surviving detached systems survive through common envelope (CE) evolution ($P_{\rm orb} \le 10\,\mathrm{yr}$). The observed NS mass distribution peaks sharply at $1.2\text{--}1.3\,M_\odot$ driven by low-kick ($\sigma = 20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) electron-capture supernovae (ECSN), while delayed core-collapse supernova (CCSN) fallback produces massive NSs exceeding $M_{\rm NS} > 2.5\,M_\odot$ in $\sim 1\%$ of systems. Pulsar spin-down and magnetic field decay follow $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = K \frac{B^2}{P_{\rm spin}}$ ($K = 9.87 \times 10^{-48}\,\mathrm{yr\,G^{-2}}$), death line $B/P_{\rm spin}^2 = 0.17 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G\,s^{-2}}$, and accretion-induced burial $B = \frac{B_0}{1 + \Delta M / (10^{-6}\,M_\odot)} \exp\left(-\frac{T - t_{\rm acc}}{\tau}\right)$ with $\tau = 3\,\mathrm{Gyr}$.
papers.problem: Quantifying the Galactic population of dormant neutron stars in detached binaries with luminous companions (NS--LC) detectable via astrometric orbital wobbles in Gaia DR4 and DR5, and testing whether their yields and orbital parameters can break degeneracies between core-collapse supernova explosion models (rapid vs. delayed), natal kicks ($\sigma = 265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs. $20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), and common envelope evolution.
papers.method: Binary population synthesis using COSMIC initialized with a Kroupa IMF ($3 < m_{\rm pri}/M_\odot < 60$), flat mass ratios ($q = m_{\rm sec}/m_{\rm pri}$), thermal eccentricities, and log-flat semi-major axes up to $10^5\,R_\odot$. Spatial distribution and star formation histories are drawn from the FIRE-2 m12i Milky Way simulation ($10^{-4} \le Z \le 0.03$). Supernova prescriptions incorporate rapid and delayed core-collapse models (maximum $M_{\rm NS} = 3\,M_\odot$), ECSN ($M_{\rm ZAMS} \sim 8\text{--}10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ch} \approx 1.38\,M_\odot$), and accretion-induced collapse (AIC), followed by synthetic observation through CCB22 and gaiamock astrometric selection functions.
papers.reason: This study models the Galactic population of dormant neutron star binaries and forecasts Gaia DR4/DR5 astrometric yields, providing quantitative constraints on core-collapse supernova engines, natal kicks, and dense matter equations of state.

papers.title: Fast X-ray Transients as Premature-Dissipated Gamma-Ray Bursts with Magnetic-Dominated Jets
papers.result: When $\sigma_0 \lesssim 45$ satisfies $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R_*) < 1$, premature Type II kink dissipation at $R_* \sim 10^{11}\ \mathrm{cm}$ produces $\Gamma \lesssim 50$ and extreme compactness $\ell' = \frac{L\sigma_{\rm T}}{4\pi R_{\rm dis} m_e c^3 \Gamma^3} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4$. Rapid thermalization through $N \sim \frac{\ln(E'_i/E'_f)}{E'_f/m_e c^2} \sim 10^3$ Compton scatterings yields a thermal soft X-ray spectrum with average photon energy $\langle E' \rangle \sim 2.7 k_{\rm B}\left(\frac{L_{\rm iso}}{4\pi R_*^2 \Gamma^2 ac}\right)^{1/4} \sim 0.7\ \mathrm{keV}$ (for $L_{\rm iso}=10^{48}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, $\Gamma \sim 20$), variability timescale $\Delta t_{\rm var} \simeq (1+z)R_{\rm ph}\theta_{\rm J}^2/(2c) \sim 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s}$, and multi-day deceleration times from $\Gamma \lesssim 10$.
papers.problem: Unifying fast X-ray transients (FXTs) with classical gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) to explain the physical origin of their low peak energy $E_{\rm peak}$, soft thermal spectra, and absence of jet breaks within massive star collapsar jets.
papers.method: A Blandford–Znajek driven Poynting-flux jet model ($\sigma_0 \equiv \dot{E}_{\rm Poynting}/\dot{E}_{\rm kinetic} \gg 1$) undergoing ideal MHD acceleration $\Gamma(R) \propto R^{1/3}$ with $\Gamma(R_*) = \sigma_0^{3/2}(R_*/R_{\rm sat})^{1/3}$, where global Type II kink dissipation is triggered by the causal connectivity criterion $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R) < 1$, followed by $e^\pm$ pair production and Compton thermalization at high compactness $\ell' \gg 1$.
papers.reason: The paper presents a unified physical framework where premature kink dissipation of Poynting-flux-dominated jets at stellar breakout naturally explains the soft thermal emission and low Lorentz factors of fast X-ray transients (FXTs) compared to classical GRBs.

papers.title: Isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux limits from Carpet-3 experiment data using neural networks with domain adaptation
papers.result: At 90% CL assuming an $E^{-2}$ spectrum, the integral diffuse gamma-ray flux upper limits span from $\Phi_{\gamma} < 3.2 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ down to $< 2.8 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ across threshold energies $14 \le \log_{10}(E/\mathrm{eV}) \le 15.75$, with proton rejection $< 1.3 \times 10^{-5}$ to $< 1 \times 10^{-3}$ and photon efficiency $\varepsilon_{\gamma}$ from $0.004$ to $0.84$. The differential flux limits $E^2 \cdot dN/dE$ range from $< 1.53 \times 10^3\,\mathrm{eV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ to $< 1.07 \times 10^2\,\mathrm{eV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ for $\log_{10}(E/\mathrm{eV}) \in [14.125, 15.875]$.
papers.problem: Measuring the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux in the $100\,\mathrm{TeV}-10\,\mathrm{PeV}$ regime to constrain the origin of astrophysical neutrinos and cosmic-ray propagation, while addressing overwhelming hadronic backgrounds and systematic mismatches between Monte-Carlo simulations and experimental data.
papers.method: Analyzed 1078 days of Carpet-3 EAS array data ($161{,}076$ preselected events with core within the $196\,\mathrm{m}^2$ array, energy release $>5000$ relativistic particles, and zenith angle $\theta \le 40^\circ$) using a neural network combining CNN and fully connected layers into a 32-dimensional latent feature vector with a gradient reversal layer ($-\lambda$) for domain adaptation. Energy-dependent selection thresholds $\xi_0$ were optimized via $\alpha = \varepsilon(\xi_0) / N_{\mathrm{bkg}}^{90}(\xi_0)$ using the Feldman-Cousins procedure, folded with effective exposure $\mathcal{E}(E) = T \int_{\Omega} A_{\mathrm{eff}}(E, \theta, \phi)\,d\Omega$ under an assumed $E^{-2}$ gamma-ray spectrum.
papers.reason: Provides upper limits on the $100\,\mathrm{TeV}-10\,\mathrm{PeV}$ isotropic diffuse gamma-ray flux using Carpet-3 EAS data, which constrains the origin of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and diffuse cosmic-ray interactions.

papers.title: The Science and Technology of Broad-Band X-ray Astrophysics
authors: The Broad-Band X-ray Science Analysis Group
papers.result: Cyclotron resonant scattering features (CRSF) in neutron star X-ray binaries fall in the $5\text{--}100\,\mathrm{keV}$ range, scaling as $E_{\rm cyc} \approx 11.6 \times (B / 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G})\,\mathrm{keV}$ and serving as the primary direct probe of surface magnetic fields from $B \sim 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G}$ up to magnetar-strength fields $B \sim 10^{14}\text{--}10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ in pulsating ultraluminous X-ray sources ($L \sim 100\,L_{\rm Edd}$); simultaneous broad-band coverage ($0.2\text{--}80\,\mathrm{keV}$) probes relativistic reflection components (Fe K line at $6\text{--}7\,\mathrm{keV}$ and Compton hump at $20\text{--}30\,\mathrm{keV}$) down to quiescent states ($L < 0.1\%\,L_{\rm Edd}$).
papers.problem: While the Cosmic X-ray Background (CXB) intensity peaks in the $20\text{--}30\,\mathrm{keV}$ band, the fraction of CXB resolved into discrete point sources collapses above $10\,\mathrm{keV}$ due to the lack of high-angular-resolution focusing hard X-ray telescopes.
papers.method: Straw-man observatory design combining nested grazing-incidence optics with focal length $f = 20\,\mathrm{m}$ and small grazing angles $\theta \sim \mathrm{mrad}$ (yielding effective area $A_{\rm eff} \approx 400\,\mathrm{cm}^2$ at $6\,\mathrm{keV}$, $300\,\mathrm{cm}^2$ at $25\,\mathrm{keV}$, and $90\,\mathrm{cm}^2$ at $70\,\mathrm{keV}$) with hybrid multilayer coatings and thick ($3\,\mathrm{mm}$) CZT/CdTe detectors covering $0.2\text{--}200\,\mathrm{keV}$.
papers.reason: This report outlines science drivers and instrument requirements for future broad-band X-ray observatories, establishing key diagnostic capabilities for compact objects, relativistic jets, and neutron star magnetic fields.

papers.title: A higher-order smoothness indicator as refinement criterion for Newtonian and relativistic MHD simulations
papers.result: The AMR criterion achieves runtime speedups of $1.45\times - 3.66\times$ across Newtonian and SRMHD benchmarks: in the Shu–Osher test, MeshBlock cycles decrease by $4.26\times$ with a $1.72\times$ speedup; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, MeshBlock cycles are reduced by $3.4\times$ with a $2.8\times$ speedup at an effective resolution of $1536^2$. In GRMHD Kerr black hole accretion simulations with spin $a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9$, the algorithm tracks turbulent MRI accretion streams and outflows in SANE ($W_{\rm max}=20$, base grid $96^3$) and successfully resolves magnetic flux eruption dynamics in MAD where the horizon dimensionless flux reaches $\phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH} / \sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$.
papers.problem: Traditional curvature-based AMR refinement criteria, such as the Löhner-type indicator, rely heavily on empirical threshold tuning and problem-dependent choice of variables, making them difficult to generalize across multi-scale relativistic MHD problems and black hole accretion environments without incurring excessive computational overhead.
papers.method: The algorithm computes the undivided fourth-order difference on a symmetric 5-point stencil ($N=4$), $\Delta^{(4)}u \equiv u_{i+2}-4u_{i+1}+6u_i-4u_{i-1}+u_{i-2}$, to define a local dimensionless oscillation measure $e_i = |\Delta^{(4)}u| / (|u_i| + \delta)$. Cells are refined when $e_i > 4^{-2} = 0.0625$, kept unchanged within $[4^{-3}, 4^{-2}]$, and coarsened when $e_i < 4^{-3} = 0.015625$. In multi-dimensional MHD implemented in AthenaK, the criterion evaluates conserved variables $(D, M^j, E, B^j)$ along all axes, automatically coarsening cells below the rest-mass density floor $D_{\boldsymbol{i}} \le D_{\mathrm{floor}}$ and using smoothing parameters $\epsilon_{\mathrm{mom}} \sim D_{\mathrm{floor}} U$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{B}} \sim (D_{\mathrm{floor}} U^2)^{1/2}$ to prevent division by zero.
papers.reason: This paper develops a dimension-free, problem-independent adaptive mesh refinement criterion based on a higher-order ($N=4$) smoothness indicator for Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations. It provides valuable numerical methodology improvements for simulating relativistic blast waves, magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, and black hole accretion flows (SANE/MAD) relevant to high-energy central engines.

papers.title: Strongly Suppressed Cosmic-Ray Diffusion in a Wind-Blown Cavity Environment of SNR G21.8-3.0
papers.result: The adjacent gamma-ray source 4FGL J1840.4-1139 (SrcT) is characterized by a curved spectrum well fitted by a Log-Parabola model with spectral index $\alpha = 0.59 \pm 0.18$ and curvature $\beta = 0.28 \pm 0.06$. Escaped cosmic rays from SNR G21.8-3.0 illuminate surrounding molecular clouds ($M \sim 101\,d_{0.8}^{2}\,M_{\odot}$, $n \sim 253\,d_{0.8}^{-1}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$), requiring an effective cosmic-ray diffusion coefficient suppressed by a factor of $\sim 30$ ($D \sim D_{\rm Gal}/30$) compared to the Galactic mean.
papers.problem: SNR G21.8-3.0 displays a non-thermal radio shell without co-spatial X-ray or gamma-ray emission, while a distinct GeV gamma-ray source is detected near the shell edge. The key issue is whether and how cosmic rays escape the shock into the progenitor wind-blown cavity and illuminate nearby molecular clouds under local magnetic and turbulent modulation.
papers.method: Performed spatial and Log-Parabola spectral analysis of 16-year *Fermi*-LAT (0.1–1000 GeV) data using Fermitools/Fermipy, coupled with PMO 13.7 m MWISP $^{12}\mathrm{CO}\,(J=1-0)$ line observations to derive molecular cloud mass ($X_{\mathrm{CO}} = 2\times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}\ K^{-1}\ km^{-1}\ s}$) and wind-bubble kinematics ($t_{\rm c} = \frac{3}{5}\frac{R_{\rm c}}{v_{\rm c}}$).
papers.reason: This study investigates cosmic-ray escape and transport within the progenitor wind-blown cavity of SNR G21.8-3.0 using combined GeV gamma-ray and CO observations. It provides direct evidence that cosmic-ray diffusion in circumstellar cavities is suppressed by a factor of ~30 relative to the canonical Galactic value.

papers.title: The Geometric Imprint of a Tilted Accretion Disk in Gravitational Waves
papers.result: During disk alignment over $10000M \leq t \leq 30000M$, the tilt angle decreases from $69.3^{\circ}$ to $13.9^{\circ}$ (reaching $\sim 9^{\circ}$ at $t=45000M$), while the gravitational wave energy fraction in higher-order modes $R_{\geq 3}$ decreases from $0.042$ to $0.011$ (reaching $0.007$ at $t=45000M$). Under the Teukolsky linear scaling relations $h_c \propto q M / D$ and $f \propto M^{-1}$ with mass ratio $q \equiv M_{\rm disk}/M$, a supermassive black hole system ($M = 5 \times 10^6 M_\odot$, $D = 4\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, $q = 0.05$) yields a characteristic strain $h_c \simeq 7.5 \times 10^{-21}$ at $f \sim 3\,\mathrm{mHz}$. The mode energy distribution follows the Wigner small $d$-matrix transformation $h_{\ell m}^{\rm geom}(t) = e^{-i m \phi_d} d^\ell_{m 0}(\theta_d) h_{\ell 0}^{\rm d}(t)$ with power allocation $p_{\ell m} = |d^\ell_{m 0}(\theta_d)|^2$.
papers.problem: How the geometric tilt and dynamic alignment of a magnetized accretion disk around a spinning Kerr black hole imprint onto multimode gravitational wave radiation and redistribute radiated energy across multipoles.
papers.method: Three-dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (3D GRMHD) simulations using AthenaK in a fixed Kerr spacetime with dimensionless spin $\chi \equiv a/M = 0.94$, simulating a Fishbone--Moncrief torus (adiabatic index $\Gamma = 4/3$, $r_{\rm in} = 10M$, $r_{\rm max} = 20M$, and magnetization $\max(p_{\rm gas})/\max(p_{\rm mag}) = 100$) coupled to the time-domain Teukolsky perturbation equation $\Psi = (r - i a \cos\theta)^4 \Psi_4 = \sum_m r^3 e^{i m \phi} \Phi_m(t, r_*, \theta)$ sourcing the total fluid and magnetic stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates the multimode gravitational wave imprint and energy redistribution of tilted accretion disks around spinning Kerr black holes using 3D GRMHD and Teukolsky formalisms. It provides valuable theoretical modeling and observable scaling relations relevant to compact object accretion dynamics and high-energy multi-messenger astrophysics.

papers.title: Constraining Accretion Heating in Neutron Stars with Carbon Instability and Quiescent Cooling
papers.result: Applying the local carbon thermonuclear instability condition $\left(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T}\right)_{P} \ge \left(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T}\right)_{P}$ strongly favors shallow accretion heating overlapping the fuel layer ($\log_{10}P=26\text{--}27\text{ dyn cm}^{-2}$) with $q_a=2.19\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ ($W=306$), whereas deep heating ($\log_{10}P=27\text{--}28\text{ dyn cm}^{-2}$) requires $q_a=4.00\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ and severely degrades the fit ($W=618$, $\Delta W \simeq 352$). When accounting for carbon nuclear burning, approximately two-thirds of the nuclear energy remains stored as thermal energy and one-third emerges as surface radiation; the superburst decay favors a depth-dependent energy distribution $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^{1/4}$ with total energy $\mathcal{E}_{\rm b} \simeq 2.2 \times 10^{42}\text{ erg}$ at $4.5\text{ kpc}$.
papers.problem: In accreting neutron stars, different crustal heating depths can produce degenerate quiescent cooling curves when heating strength and core temperature are adjusted independently, obscuring the physical location of shallow accretion heating.
papers.method: Thermal evolution and crustal transport simulations incorporating conductive cooling $\epsilon_{\rm cool} = 0.17 \frac{K\rho T}{y^2}$, accretion heating $\epsilon_{a}=\frac{\dot{M}Q_{a}}{M_{a}m_{u}}$, carbon ignition criteria, parameterized superburst energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^{\beta}$ (with $\beta=0$ or $1/4$), and Nelder–Mead simplex optimization against 10 Chandra quiescent spectra ($0.5\text{--}7\text{ keV}$).
papers.reason: The paper provides key physical constraints on neutron star shallow crustal heating by jointly combining carbon thermonuclear ignition criteria with quiescent cooling observations of KS 1731-260.

papers.title: Probing the Turbulent Magnetised Interstellar Medium of the Small Magellanic Cloud through Depolarisation with POSSUM Observations
papers.result: The fraction of polarized sources is significantly suppressed on-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$) compared to off-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), accompanied by an enhanced Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 74 \pm 9\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$. Modeling external Faraday dispersion with Burn's law gives $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.32$, implying a tangled random magnetic field strength $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)\,(l_0/0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ ($B_r \approx 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ at the beam scale $\sim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$).
papers.problem: Determining whether depolarization of background radio sources in the SMC is driven by small-scale thermal electron density fluctuations or turbulent random magnetic fields, and assessing whether small-scale Faraday dispersion matches extrapolations of the large-scale RM power spectrum.
papers.method: Subtracted SMC diffuse emission, performed RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting on POSSUM Pilot II data ($800-1088\ \mathrm{MHz}$), and modeled external Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = 0.812\,n_e\,B_\parallel\,\sqrt{l_0\,L} = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ combined with $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-derived emission measure $\left(\frac{\mathrm{EM}}{\mathrm{cm^{-6}\ pc}}\right) \approx 2.75 \left(\frac{I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha,\mathrm{corr}}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \left(\frac{T_e}{10^4\ \mathrm{K}}\right)^{0.942}$.
papers.reason: This paper uses ASKAP POSSUM broadband polarization observations to probe statistical depolarization and Faraday dispersion across the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). It provides valuable empirical constraints on the turbulent magneto-ionic medium and thermal electron density scaling in dwarf irregular galaxies, relevant to intervening sightlines and propagation effects of extragalactic transients.

papers.title: WFST0533buha (Bi'an): A Fast Blue Ultraluminous Transient Candidate with Unusual Blue/NUV Colors
papers.result: The transient brightened by $\Delta u \approx 2.45 \pm 0.11\,\mathrm{mag}$ in $\sim 3\,\mathrm{d}$ with rise and decline half-maximum timescales $t_{1/2,\mathrm{rise}} = 2.20^{+0.10}_{-0.09}\,\mathrm{d}$ and $t_{1/2,\mathrm{dec}} = 3.39^{+0.21}_{-0.20}\,\mathrm{d}$ ($t_{1/2} < 6\,\mathrm{d}$), reaching peak absolute magnitudes $M_u = -20.68$, $M_g = -20.62$, and $M_r = -20.21$ at reference $z=0.25$. Over $0.05 \le z \le 0.30$, blackbody fits yield temperatures $T_{\mathrm{BB}} \sim (1.7\text{--}2.2) \times 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$, photosphere radii $R_{\mathrm{BB}} \sim (0.28\text{--}1.28) \times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$, and bolometric luminosities $L_{\mathrm{bol}} \sim 5.1 \times 10^{42}\text{--}2.5 \times 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, with optical $gr$ blackbody extrapolation overpredicting $u$-band flux by $\sim 0.24\,\mathrm{mag}$. Multiwavelength observations reveal a faint $15\,\mathrm{GHz}$ radio counterpart with peak flux density $24.8 \pm 4.7\,\mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$ and an EP/FXT X-ray upper limit $F_X < 3.3 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: The combination of high optical peak luminosity ($M_g \lesssim -20\,\mathrm{mag}$) and extremely short rise and decay timescales cannot be reconciled with conventional $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$-decay powered supernova models, while the nature of the event is observationally hindered by an unknown spectroscopic redshift.
papers.method: Multi-band $ugr$ PSF photometry from the WFST DHugr survey and Subaru/FOCAS corrected for Galactic extinction ($E(B-V)=0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, $R_V=3.1$), Gaussian Process light-curve regression, Gemini-S GMOS-S low-resolution spectroscopy, absorbed power-law modeling of Einstein Probe/FXT X-ray non-detections ($n_{\mathrm{H}}=3.54 \times 10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, $\Gamma=1.5$), and MCMC blackbody fitting over the trial redshift range $0.05 \le z \le 0.30$.
papers.reason: WFST0533buha (Bi'an) is a newly discovered fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT) candidate exhibiting rapid optical evolution and an unusual blue/NUV color deficit, offering important empirical constraints on FBUT diversity and central engine/circumstellar interaction models.

papers.title: Possible origins of the two γ-ray components C0 and C1 in IC 443
papers.result: For compact component C0, the SNR-MC hadronic model reproduces the observed SED with a clear $\pi^0$-decay peak, yielding a proton injection spectral index $s = 2.03$, diffusion suppression factor $\chi = 0.08$, and momentum cutoff $p_{\rm cut} = 5.0\times 10^5\text{ GeV}/c$, confirming C0 as a potential Galactic PeVatron candidate. For extended component C1, leptonic inverse Compton scattering from PWN CXOU J061705.3+222127 electrons reproduces the emission with spin-down luminosity $L_{\rm age} = 1.0\times 10^{36}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$, magnetic field $B_{\rm age} = 4.7\ \mu\text{G}$, electron injection index $s = 1.90$, and energy cutoff $E_{\rm cut} = 1.75\times 10^5\text{ GeV}$, requiring strongly suppressed diffusion $D_1 = 1\times 10^{26}\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$ with Bohm scaling $\delta = 1$, identifying C1 as a candidate TeV halo.
papers.problem: Disentangling the distinct physical origins and radiation mechanisms of the compact component C0 and the extended component C1 (angular scale $\sim 0.67^\circ$) in the middle-aged supernova remnant IC 443.
papers.method: The authors apply two independent transport and emission models: (1) An SNR-MC hadronic model for C0 accounting for diffusive shock acceleration and energy-dependent proton escape with spectrum $N_{\rm esc}(p) = N_0 p_{\rm br,1}^{-\beta/\alpha} p^{-s}$ ($p \le p_{\rm br,1}$) and $N_0 p^{-(s+\beta/\alpha)} \exp(-p/p_{\rm cut})$ ($p > p_{\rm br,1}$), integrated over a molecular cloud shell $F(p) = \eta \int_{L_1}^{L_2} f(t_{\rm age}, r, p) 4\pi r^2 dr$ with $\beta = 3(3-s)/2$ and $\alpha = 6.5$. (2) A spherically symmetric multi-zone leptonic Fokker-Planck transport model for C1 incorporating spatial diffusion $D(p) = 10^{28}\chi (cp/10\text{ GeV})^\delta\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$, advection, and radiative cooling $\dot{E}_{e,\rm rad} = \frac{4}{3}\sigma_{\rm T} c \left(\frac{E_e}{m_e c^2}\right)^2 [U_B + U_{\rm rad}]$ from the central pulsar wind nebula.
papers.reason: This paper investigates the dual gamma-ray components of middle-aged SNR IC 443 detected by LHAASO, modeling hadronic emission from SNR-molecular cloud interactions and leptonic emission from the associated PWN, providing direct constraints on Galactic cosmic-ray acceleration and TeV halo formation.

papers.title: A lepto-hadronic perspective on the properties of the candidate neutrino-emitter blazar 5BZQ J0808+4950
papers.problem: The emission mechanism governing the second SED hump in blazars and the physical viability of 5BZQ J0808+4950 producing detectable high-energy neutrinos coincident with IC110929A remain debated.
papers.method: A time-dependent lepto-hadronic code (AM3) is applied to a spherical blob moving at relativistic speed $\beta_{\mathrm{j}}=\sqrt{1-\Gamma_{\mathrm{j}}^{-2}}$ with $\delta_{\mathrm{j}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{j}}$, continuous particle injection $Q^{\prime}_{i}(E^{\prime}_{i}) \propto E^{\prime -p_{i}}_{i} \exp\left[-(E^{\prime}_{i}/E^{\prime}_{i,\mathrm{max}})^{2}\right]$, particle escape time $t_{\mathrm{esc}}=R^{\prime}_{\mathrm{blob}}/c$, and external radiation fields from the accretion disk ($L_{\mathrm{disk}}=0.1\dot{M}c^{2}$) and broad-line region ($L_{\mathrm{BLR}}=0.1L_{\mathrm{disk}}$).
papers.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch lepto-hadronic SED modeling of the candidate neutrino-emitter blazar 5BZQ J0808+4950, revealing that X-ray luminosity serves as a more reliable observational proxy for neutrino emission than gamma-rays.

papers.title: Interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimation for fast radio burst cosmology
papers.result: On 120 localized FRBs ($z \le 2.148$), AttNPE reproduces MCMC posteriors with Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathrm{JSD} < 0.0043$, measuring the IGM dispersion amplitude $\mathcal{A} = 3.221^{+0.224}_{-0.232}\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ (MCMC: $3.229^{+0.209}_{-0.224}\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$) while generating $5\times 10^4$ posterior samples in $0.03\,\mathrm{s}$ on GPU. Independent simulation validation yields well-calibrated posteriors (KS test $p > 0.05$ for marginal PP and joint TARP metrics), showing that sources at $0.3 \le z < 0.7$ contribute $46.2\%$ of total attention weight and $>40\%$ of shifts in $\Omega_{\rm m}$, $\Omega_{\rm b}$, and $H_0$.
papers.problem: Traditional Bayesian MCMC inference for FRB cosmology suffers from severe computational bottlenecks due to repeated numerical convolutions over Galactic halo, host galaxy, and IGM dispersion distributions, and standard neural estimators lack physical interpretability regarding how individual bursts at various redshifts constrain cosmological parameters.
papers.method: Combines a permutation-invariant attention encoder with a conditional masked autoregressive flow (MAF) to infer 7 parameters $\bm{\theta} = \{\Omega_{\rm m}, \Omega_{\rm b}, H_0, f_{\rm d}, F, \mu_{\rm host}, \sigma_{\rm host}\}$ from the extragalactic dispersion measure $\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm E},i} = \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm obs},i}-\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm ISM},i} = \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm halo},i}+\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm IGM},i}+\frac{\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm host},i}}{1+z_i}$, with $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}(z)\rangle = \frac{3cH_{0}\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}}{8\pi Gm_{p}}\int_{0}^{z}\frac{\chi_{e}(z^{\prime})(1+z^{\prime})}{E(z^{\prime})}\,\mathrm{d}z^{\prime}$, trained dynamically on $10^6$ simulated catalogs conditioned on single-source likelihoods $p_i(\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm E},i}|z_i,\bm{\theta})=\int\mathrm{d}\mathrm{DM}_{\rm halo}\int\mathrm{d}\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}\,p_{\rm halo}p_{\rm host}p_{\rm IGM}$.
papers.reason: The paper develops AttNPE, an attention-based neural posterior estimation framework that drastically accelerates cosmological parameter inference from localized FRB dispersion measures while providing redshift-dependent interpretability.

papers.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
papers.result: Joint multi-probe inference yields a canonical neutron star radius $R_{1.4}=11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83}\,\mathrm{km}$ and maximum non-rotating mass $M_{\rm max}=2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23}\,M_{\odot}$ (90% credibility), favoring EoSs like GMSR_H4_BSK24 over softer models.
papers.problem: Constraining the neutron star equation of state across multiple density regimes by combining gravitational waves, X-ray pulse profiles, and radio pulsar timing without the prohibitive cost of full EoS-dependent parameter estimation.
papers.method: Extends the GWXtreme framework to perform joint Bayesian inference across GW ($(\mathcal{M}, q, \tilde{\Lambda})$), NICER ($M$-$R$), and radio pulsars ($M_{\rm max}$) by re-weighting EoS-independent posterior samples via Gaussian kernel density estimation (KDE) on EoS-defined hypersurfaces.
papers.reason: Directly relevant to compact object high-energy astrophysics by constraining the neutron star equation of state and maximum mass, which govern central engines in explosive transients.

papers.title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
papers.result: The infrared spectrum of Pa30's central star is modeled by a non-LTE stellar wind with luminosity $L = 3.6 \times 10^4\,L_{\odot}$ ($10^{4.6}\,L_\odot$), effective radius $R_{*}(\tau=2.3) = 0.136\,R_{\odot}$, mass-loss rate $\dot{M} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, and terminal wind velocity $V_{\infty} \sim 15{,}000\text{--}16{,}000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in a C/O/Ne-dominated atmosphere ($Y_{\mathrm{O}}=0.41, Y_{\mathrm{Ne}}=0.44, Y_{\mathrm{C}}=0.13$). The near-infrared emission is dominated by hydrogenic $\mathrm{O\,VI}$ transitions ($n \rightarrow n-1$), including a $1.12\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ P Cygni profile ($3p\,^2\mathrm{P}^o - 3d\,^2\mathrm{D}$), where dielectronic recombination of $\mathrm{O\,V}$ at $T \sim 20{,}000\,\mathrm{K}$ with rate coefficient $\alpha_{\mathrm{dr}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{cm}^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ dominates radiative recombination ($\alpha_{\mathrm{rr}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-12}\,\mathrm{cm}^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$). High-ionization emission lines are successfully reproduced by a collisionally ionized coronal plasma model.
papers.problem: Unveiling the infrared spectral properties and wind ionization mechanism of the extremely hot, hydrogen- and helium-deficient central star of SN 1181 remnant Pa30, which had no prior infrared spectral observations to constrain its mass loss and line-formation physics.
papers.method: Combined space-based spectroscopy from SPHEREx ($0.75\text{--}5.0\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \sim 35\text{--}41$) with high-resolution ground-based NIR spectra from Gemini North GNIRS ($R \sim 1{,}200$), TNG NICS ($R = 500$), and DOT TANSPEC ($R \sim 1{,}600$). Data were reduced using pixel-fitting quality metrics $\mathrm{fit}_{\mathrm{ql}}=\langle |p_k - m_k|/\sigma_k \rangle$ to isolate the central point source, and modeled via non-LTE comoving-frame radiative transfer using CMFGEN alongside collisionally ionized coronal plasma simulations with CLOUDY.
papers.reason: This work presents the first infrared spectroscopic investigation and wind radiative transfer modeling of Pa30, the bound compact remnant of the Type Iax supernova SN 1181. It provides key empirical wind parameters and ionization constraints directly relevant to surviving central engines of deflagration supernovae.

papers.title: Deconstructing the cosmic baryon distribution with fast radio bursts
papers.result: The reconstruction recovers the total cosmic electron budget within $1.4\%$ ($\\langle r_{\mathrm{FRB}}\\rangle_M = (0.986 \pm 0.005)\,r_{\mathrm{theo}}$ with theoretical reference $r_{\mathrm{theo}} \approx (7.84 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$) and measures the ionized baryon density $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (matching the simulation ground truth of $0.0462$ within $0.2\sigma$, corresponding to $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.95$). Gas mass fractions across large-scale structure environments are determined to be $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{void}} = 0.186 \pm 0.012$, $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{filament}} = 0.179 \pm 0.015$, and $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.046 \pm 0.014$, showing that $\sim 75\%$ of free electrons reside in low-density regimes with $\rho_{\mathrm{m}}/\rho_{\mathrm{crit}} \le 2.94$.
papers.problem: Disentangling the continuous, multi-phase spatial distribution of diffuse cosmic baryons across the cosmic web (voids, filaments, haloes) from one-dimensional integrated FRB dispersion measures $\mathrm{DM} = \int n_{\mathrm{e}} (1+z)^{-1} \mathrm{d}l$ to resolve the missing baryon problem.
papers.method: Coupling IllustrisTNG (TNG300-1) MHD simulations with Euclid-like mock galaxy catalogues; partitioning continuous matter density fields into $M = 8$ logarithmic density bins; formulating an overdetermined linear inverse problem $\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{r} + \mathbf{n}$ for the electron-to-matter density ratio $r = n_{\mathrm{e}}/\rho$ parameterized by a four-parameter skewed profile $f(x)$ with MCMC sampling (`emcee`) and filtering redundant sightlines via slice density correlation $|R_{ij}| < 0.3$.
papers.reason: This paper presents a forward-modeling and Bayesian reconstruction framework to deconstruct FRB dispersion measures into density regimes of the cosmic web, providing quantitative constraints on missing baryons in diffuse IGM/WHIM phases.
