papers.title: FAST Burst-Cluster Catalog of FRB 20240114A
papers.result: The catalog comprises $13261$ burst clusters, $19037$ bursts, and $29026$ sub-bursts over $495$ days ($58.83$ hr exposure in 99 sessions). A weighted linear fit yields a secular DM increase rate of $\dot{\mathrm{DM}} = 1.29 \pm 0.11~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, while single-day DM shows an intra-day median of $528.4~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ (IQR $528.1$--$528.8~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$), confirming that broad single-day DM spreads in literature are morphology-induced pseudo-DM. Downward-to-upward drifting cluster ratio is $\approx 9.4:1$ with median drifting rates $R_{\rm d} = -27.7~\mathrm{MHz\,ms^{-1}}$ (D2-M) and $7.0~\mathrm{MHz\,ms^{-1}}$ (U2-M). Waiting times follow a three-component log-normal distribution with characteristic timescales $e^\mu \approx 2.34~\mathrm{ms}$, $24.83~\mathrm{ms}$, and $7.57~\mathrm{s}$ (inter-cluster, $\delta > 0.4~\mathrm{s}$), where cluster arrivals align with a variable-rate Poisson process. Characteristic emission frequencies correlate between FAST and Parkes ($r = 0.56, p = 5.3 \times 10^{-5}$) across a $112.91$-day modulation. Normalized burst cluster energy scales monotonically with multiplicity $N_{\rm sub}$ (Spearman $\rho = 0.895$--$1.000$), with higher energies observed during active phases and in complex/downward-drifting morphologies.
papers.problem: Investigating the hierarchical multi-timescale emission morphology, spectral-temporal drifting physics, burst energetics, and distinguishing true secular circum-burst DM evolution from morphology-induced pseudo-DM in the active repeating source FRB 20240114A.
papers.method: Analysis of 495-day monitoring using FAST L-band 19-beam receiver (center beam), utilizing TransientX and PSRCHIVE for pulse search and data reduction. Bursts within a $400~\mathrm{ms}$ window are grouped into burst clusters, followed by manual DM optimization in steps of $0.1~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ for $N_{\rm sub} \geq 2$ clusters, coupled with Weibull and log-normal waiting-time statistics.
papers.reason: This paper establishes the largest FAST burst-cluster catalog for the active repeating FRB 20240114A, providing vital empirical constraints on local magneto-ionic environment evolution (secular $\dot{\mathrm{DM}}$) and multi-timescale burst clustering directly relevant to repeating FRB central engines and PRS interactions.

papers.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
papers.result: For typical parameters ($v_{\mathrm{sh}} \sim 0.1\,c$, $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 10^{-4}\,M_\odot$, $r_{\mathrm{out}} = 10^{13}\,\mathrm{cm}$), thermal coupling yields $\eta \approx 4$ and a Comptonized color temperature $T_{\mathrm{col,SBO}} \approx 0.127\,\mathrm{keV}$, naturally generating soft X-ray transients with peak luminosities $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{45}-10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. MCMC modeling of EP260321a ($z=0.0344$) reproduces its observed peak luminosity of $(1.0\pm 0.3)\times 10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $(690\pm 60)\,\mathrm{s}$ with blackbody temperature $\sim 0.1-0.13\,\mathrm{keV}$, establishing it as the first confirmed non-relativistic shock breakout EFXT.
papers.problem: Investigates whether shock breakout and post-breakout cooling emission in a pre-explosion dense circumstellar material shell can comprehensively explain extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) like EP260321a, XRF 060218, and XRO 080109 without invoking relativistic jets.
papers.method: Constructs a semi-analytical radiation-mediated shock model in a spherical thin CSM shell ($M_{\mathrm{CSM}}$, $r_{\mathrm{out}}$, $\chi \equiv (r_{\mathrm{out}}-r_{\mathrm{in}})/r_{\mathrm{out}} \ll 1$, $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim M_{\mathrm{CSM}}/(4\pi r_{\mathrm{out}}^3 \chi)$) driven by SN ejecta with shock velocity $v_{\mathrm{sh}} \approx 0.1\,E_{\mathrm{kin},51}^{1/2}(M_{\mathrm{ej}}/2\,M_\odot)^{-5/14}(M_{\mathrm{CSM}}/10^{-4}\,M_\odot)^{-1/7}c$. Incorporates non-LTE Comptonization color-temperature correction ($T_{\mathrm{col}} = T_{\mathrm{BB}}\eta^2/\xi^2$ when coupling parameter $\eta \approx n_{\mathrm{BB}}/[t_{\mathrm{diff}}\dot{n}_{\mathrm{ph,ff}}(T_{\mathrm{BB}})] > 1$) and integrates over equal-arrival-time surfaces $t = t_{\mathrm{obs}} - [\max(r_{\mathrm{out}}, r_{\mathrm{sh}})/c](1-\cos\theta)$ to account for light-travel time effects.
papers.reason: Directly investigates supernova shock breakout and cooling emission in dense circumstellar material shells to model extragalactic fast X-ray transients such as EP260321a, aligning directly with the group's core focus on shock breakout and CSM interaction.

papers.title: Multimessenger constraints on the origin of long gamma-ray bursts with plateaus: three cases
papers.result: MCMC fitting of X-ray plateaus under the collapsar black hole spin-down model yields initial black hole masses $M_{\rm BH} \sim 24\text{--}124\,M_{\odot}$ and accretion disc masses $M_{\rm disc} \sim 0.1\,M_{\rm BH}$ (e.g., GRB 080319C has $M_0 = 123.5 \pm 3.7\,M_{\odot}$, $\log_{10}(\dot{M}/[M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}]) = -1.83 \pm 0.03$, $M_{\mathrm{disc}} = 12.0 \pm 0.8\,M_{\odot}$). In a pessimistic scenario (efficiency $\epsilon = 0.1$), the characteristic gravitational wave strains at $\sim 200\,\mathrm{Hz}$ are $h_c \sim (1.5\text{--}1.84) \times 10^{-24}$, placing them on the detection threshold of Cosmic Explorer with an expected detection rate of $0.5\text{--}1.5\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. In contrast, a white dwarf tidal disruption event (WD-TDE) around an intermediate-mass black hole ($M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^5\,M_{\odot}$) emits at $f_{\rm peak} \simeq 1.6 f_c = \frac{1.6}{2\pi}\sqrt{G M_{\rm BH}/r_t^3} < 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, falling in the decihertz band detectable by DECIGO/BBO.
papers.problem: The identity and energy-injection mechanism of the central engines powering long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with X-ray plateaus—specifically whether they are driven by accreting/non-accreting magnetars or Kerr black holes via accretion and Blandford-Znajek spin-down—remain degenerate from electromagnetic observations alone.
papers.method: The authors model collapsar black hole evolution governed by coupled accretion and Blandford-Znajek torque equations, $\frac{dM_{\rm BH}}{dt} = e_{\rm in}\dot{M} - \frac{L_{\rm BZ}}{c^2}$ and $\frac{da}{dt} = \frac{c}{G M_{\rm BH}^2}(l_{\rm in}\dot{M} - T_{\rm BZ})$, distinguishing turbulent disc broadband emission (Model A) from descending chirps (Model B) and magnetar spin-down (Model C). Black hole parameters are derived via MCMC fitting of Swift/XRT afterglow light curves and mapped to GW strain spectra $h_c(f)$ for 3G ground-based and space-borne detectors.
papers.reason: This work directly investigates the central engine nature of long GRBs with X-ray plateaus by distinguishing collapsar black holes from magnetars using multimessenger gravitational wave signatures and accretion evolution.

papers.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.result: Current LVK O4 subsolar searches suffer severe detection losses for collapsar-origin NS-BH binaries due to early tidal disruption and waveform dephasing, yielding an event detection fraction $\epsilon = ({\rm FF}\times B)^3 \sim 10^{-2}$ for light neutron stars ($m_{\rm NS} \simeq 0.1\,M_\odot$). Consequently, the actual merger rate upper limit $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon$ is weakened by several orders of magnitude compared to published point-mass bounds, matching the long gamma-ray burst rate $\mathcal{R}_0 \simeq 80\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ only near chirp mass $\mathcal{M}_c \simeq 2\,M_\odot$.
papers.problem: Standard stellar evolution cannot produce remnant black holes or core-collapse neutron stars below $M_{\mathrm{Ch}} \simeq 1.45\,M_\odot\,(Y_e/0.5)^2$, leaving the origin and observational detectability of potential subsolar-mass compact binaries in collapsar disks unconstrained by standard point-mass templates.
papers.method: A frequency-domain TaylorF2 post-Newtonian model $\tilde{h}_{\texttt{NSBHc}}(f;\bm{\theta}) = \tilde{h}_{0}(f;\bm{\theta})\,\mathcal{S}_{*}(f;\bm{\theta})\,\mathcal{S}_{\text{end}}(f;\bm{\theta})\exp[{\rm i}\,\delta\psi(f;\bm{\theta})]$ is constructed, incorporating window functions and phase corrections $\delta\psi = \delta\psi_{\rm env}+\delta\psi_{\rm ecc}+\delta\psi_{\rm SIQM}+\delta\psi_{\rm tidal}$. Crucial dynamical corrections include Type I gas migration ($-4$PN) $\delta\psi_{\rm env} = -\frac{25C_{\rm I}}{2496\pi}\frac{f_{\rm disk}\dot{M}_{\rm BH}}{\alpha\mathbb{H}^4}v^{-8}\psi_{\rm N}$, residual eccentricity ($-19/6$PN), spin-induced quadrupole moments (2PN), and tidal deformability (5PN).
papers.reason: The paper investigates gravitational waveform modeling and observational detectability for subsolar-mass NS-BH binaries formed via collapsar accretion disk fragmentation, which directly relates to supernova central engines and long gamma-ray burst progenitor environments.

papers.title: Intra-day variability of the gamma-ray/optical emission of 3C 454.3: the complexity beyond the long-term correlation
papers.problem: Investigating whether the strong long-term optical/$\gamma$-ray correlation in blazar 3C 454.3 holds on intra-day timescales ($\le 24\,\mathrm{h}$) and testing canonical single-zone leptonic models (EC vs. SSC) against multi-zone or structured jet scenarios.
papers.method: Combined 17-year Fermi-LAT and AGILE-GRID ($0.1-10\,\mathrm{GeV}$) observations with optical $R$-band photometry from WEBT; modeled $\gamma$-ray spectra with a log-parabola $\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}E}(E) = N_{0}\left(\frac{E}{E_{b}}\right)^{-\left[\alpha+\beta\ln\left(E/E_{b}\right)\right]}$ with $E_b = 908\,\mathrm{MeV}$, evaluated Spearman correlation coefficients $\rho_S$, fitted power-law scaling $L_{\gamma}\propto L_{R}^{\eta}$, and mapped the evolution of the Compton dominance $\mathrm{CD}$.
papers.reason: This paper presents a 17-year multi-wavelength analysis of 3C 454.3 showing that the long-term optical/gamma-ray correlation breaks down into epoch-dependent behavior on sub-day timescales, directly constraining relativistic jet emission mechanisms and multi-zone structures.

papers.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.result: Using 125 localized FRBs at $0.105 \le z \le 2.148$, the authors obtain $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ in the flat $w$CDM model with BBN priors. In flat $\Lambda$CDM, $H_0 = 66.49^{+6.99}_{-6.43}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.27^{+0.09}_{-0.07}$. In flat $w_0 w_a$CDM, $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.33 \pm 0.10$, $w_0 = -0.65^{+0.43}_{-0.57}$, and $w_a = -0.78^{+1.26}$. The $\Omega_{\rm m}-w$ parameter degeneracy shows a positive correlation coefficient of $+0.54$, orthogonal to SNe Ia ($-0.94$), because increasing $\Omega_{\rm m}$ reduces $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}\rangle$ while enhancing $\sigma_{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}}$, whereas increasing $w$ reduces both.
papers.problem: Deriving robust, standalone cosmological parameter constraints on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and $w$ using only localized FRBs without relying on external SNe Ia, BAO, or CMB measurements, while accounting for cosmic variance and host galaxy dispersion measure contributions.
papers.method: Bayesian inference with PyMultiNest on 125 localized FRBs ($0.105 \le z \le 2.148$) with selection cuts $z > 0.1$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm exgal} > 5\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$. Total DM is decomposed as $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm obs}(z) = \mathrm{DM}_{\rm MW,ISM} + \mathrm{DM}_{\rm MW,halo} + \mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}(z) + \frac{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}}{1+z}$, where $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}(z_s)\rangle = \int_0^{z_s} \frac{c W(z)\,\mathrm{d}z}{H(z)}$ with weight function $W(z) = \frac{3\Omega_b H_0^2 \chi_e f_{\rm d}(z)(1+z)}{8\pi G m_p}$ (calibrated via TNG300) and variance $\sigma_{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}}^2(z_s) \simeq \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{z_s} \frac{c\,\mathrm{d}z}{H(z)} W^2(z) \int_0^\infty \mathrm{d}k\,k\,P_{ee}(k,z)$ under the Limber and flat-sky approximations.
papers.reason: The paper provides the first joint measurement of the cosmic matter density $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and dark energy equation of state $w$ using exclusively localized FRB dispersion measures, directly advancing FRB dispersion modeling and cosmological applications.

papers.title: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
papers.result: Candidate short periods such as $P \sim 1.78\text{ s}$ with nominal Poisson significance of $3.62\sigma$ in FRB 20201124A (and conflicting peaks reaching up to $5.2\sigma$) clustering around $1\text{--}10\text{ s}$ across four active repeaters (FRB 20121102A, FRB 20201124A, FRB 20220912A, and FRB 20240114A) are reproduced by time-shuffled surrogate sequences preserving empirical waiting-time statistics. In ETAS simulations, varying the injected rotation period does not shift the recovered candidate recurrence distribution, showing that standard Poisson false-alarm calibration $p_{\rm FAP} = N_{\rm sim}(S_{\rm max} \geq S_{\rm obs}) / N_{\rm sim}$ severely overestimates detection significance.
papers.problem: Whether reported second-scale candidate periodicities (e.g., $P \sim 1.78\text{ s}$) in repeating FRBs represent true magnetar spin modulation or spurious artifacts generated by burst clustering and non-Poisson waiting-time distributions under sliding-window searches.
papers.method: Applied unbinned Rayleigh statistics $Z_{m}^{2}(P) = \frac{2}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{m}\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\cos k\phi_{i}\right)^{2} + \left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sin k\phi_{i}\right)^{2}\right]$ with phase folding $\phi_{i} = \frac{(t_{i}-t_{0}) \bmod P}{P}$ and de Jager $H$-test $H(P) = \max_{1 \leq m \leq 5}[Z_{m}^{2}(P) - 4m + 4]$ across sliding windows of $N = 20\text{--}30$ bursts in the period range $0.01\text{ s} \leq P \leq 100\text{ s}$, combined with $10^{7}$ homogeneous Poisson Monte Carlo runs ($p_{\rm single} = \exp(-Z_{1}^{2}/2)$), model-independent waiting-time randomization, and Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) point-process simulations.
papers.reason: This study critically assesses candidate second-scale periodicities in repeating FRBs and demonstrates that non-Poissonian burst clustering and waiting-time statistics spuriously mimic coherent periodic signals.

papers.title: New Candidate Activity Periods from FRB 20240209A and Repeating Fast Radio Burst Sources in the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.result: Identified a candidate activity period of $P = 170.4 \pm 4.7\ \mathrm{days}$ ($5.3\sigma$ post-trials) for FRB 20240209A with duty cycle $\delta = 0.89 \pm 0.02$ and active phase window $\phi = 0.34\text{--}0.76$ (enclosing $75\%$ of bursts within $42\%$ of the cycle), ruling out the previously reported $128.5\ \mathrm{day}$ period at $5.5\sigma$, while finding its period derivative $\dot{P} = 0.20 \pm 0.04\ \mathrm{day\ day^{-1}}$ very tentative. Uncovered three additional candidate periods from CHIME/FRB Catalog 2: FRB 20190208A with $P = 28.46 \pm 0.08\ \mathrm{days}$ ($3.1\sigma$, $\delta = 0.646 \pm 0.002$), FRB 20200926A with $P = 86.7 \pm 0.5\ \mathrm{days}$ ($4.0\sigma$, $\delta = 0.162 \pm 0.001$), and FRB 20220529A with $P = 36.4 \pm 0.5\ \mathrm{days}$ ($3.5\sigma$), alongside confirming FRB 20180916B at $P = 16.335 \pm 0.008\ \mathrm{days}$ ($13.8\sigma$, $\dot{P} = -1.3^{+4.0}_{-4.0} \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{day\ day^{-1}}$).
papers.problem: Investigating whether long-term periodic bursting activity is a generic property of repeating FRBs, testing physical mechanisms (neutron star precession, binary orbital modulation, or intrinsic magnetar active episodes), and resolving ambiguities caused by sparse arrival times and survey exposure window aliasing.
papers.method: Implemented a periodicity search pipeline across trial frequency range $[f_{\mathrm{min}}, f_{\mathrm{max}}] = [3/T, 1/P_{\mathrm{min}}]$ ($P_{\mathrm{min}} = 10\ \mathrm{days}$, oversampling factor $O = 5$) using Lomb-Scargle, weighted Rayleigh ($Z_1^2$), and weighted $H$-test statistics; assessed significance via $N_{\mathrm{sim}} = 10^9$ Monte Carlo simulations under an exposure-modulated homogeneous Poisson null model, with aliasing evaluated via $f_{\mathrm{alias}} = |f \pm m f_{\mathrm{sid}}|$ and exposure window power at $f_{\mathrm{w}} = 1/(306.6\ \mathrm{days})$.
papers.reason: This paper presents systematic searches for periodic activity in repeating FRBs using the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 and targeted observations of FRB 20240209A, uncovering four candidate activity periods that constrain repeating FRB progenitor models and emission geometry.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.result: The endgame collapse of the neutron star proceeds under near-free-fall contraction with radius $R_{\rm NS} \propto \Delta t^{2/3}$, driving a steep magnetic dipole luminosity surge $L_{\rm md} \propto \Delta t^{-4}$ with horizon hair-loss cutoff within $\mathcal{O}(10)\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Total energy output reaches $E_{\rm GRB} \sim 10^{48}\,(\epsilon_M/0.1)(B_p/10^{16}\,\mathrm{G})^2\,\mathrm{erg}$ from magnetospheric release and up to $E_{\rm GRB} \sim 3\times 10^{49}\,(\eta_T/0.1)(\Omega(0)/10^4\,\mathrm{s}^{-1})^{9/2}\,\mathrm{erg}$ from buoyant toroidal flux reconnection, potentially accompanied by an FRB with $E_{\rm FRB} \sim 10^{44}\,(B_p/10^{16}\,\mathrm{G})^2\,\mathrm{erg}$.
papers.problem: Whether the endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star by an asteroid-mass primordial black hole can produce a short gamma-ray burst without forming an accretion disk.
papers.method: Theoretical modeling of relativistic Bondi accretion inside a neutron star ($\\dot{M}_{\rm PBH} \propto M_{\rm PBH}^2$) coupled with differential rotation and magnetic field amplification, deriving the radiation dynamics during near-free-fall collapse where $R_{\rm NS} \propto \Delta t^{2/3}$ and $L_{\rm md} \propto \Delta t^{-4}$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates a novel diskless engine mechanism where PBH consumption of a neutron star powers short GRBs and coherent radio bursts. This provides an alternative physical channel for compact object transients and GRB central engine models.

papers.title: Periodicities of small regular jet deviations in SS433 and their origin
papers.result: The mean relativistic jet speed is $\bar{\beta} = 0.2562 \pm 0.0004$, exhibiting orbital modulation at $P = 13.083\,\mathrm{d}$ with velocity amplitude $\Delta\beta = (6.0 \pm 0.6) \times 10^{-3}$ (peaking at orbital phase $\varphi = 0.334 \pm 0.015$) and a combination frequency $(\omega+2\Omega)$ modulation at $P = 11.267\,\mathrm{d}$ with $\Delta\beta = (4.5 \pm 0.5) \times 10^{-3}$. Directional deviations exhibit periodicities in redshift at $P = 6.2870\,\mathrm{d}$ (nutation, $\Delta z = (9.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$), $P = 5.8342\,\mathrm{d}$ ($(2\omega+3\Omega)$, $\Delta z = (3.2 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$), and a newly detected period at $P = 3.0830\,\mathrm{d}$ ($(4\omega+3\Omega)$, $\Delta z = (2.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$). The line-of-sight velocity perturbation scales as $\Delta z \approx \gamma\beta a(\mu) \mathbf{d}\cdot\mathbf{I} = \gamma\beta \sum_{k} a_k \mu^k \cos(\varphi - \varphi_k) \sin i$.
papers.problem: Relativistic jets in SS433 systematically deviate from standard kinematic precession and nutation models, exhibiting both independent random angular jitter ($\sigma \lesssim 1.5^{\circ}$) breaking strict antiparallelism and harmonic velocity/directional periodicities whose dynamical origins require quantitative explanation.
papers.method: Analysis of 461 optical spectra ($3550\text{--}7450\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) obtained with the Caucasus Mountain Observatory 2.5-m telescope (2020–2026) across Balmer and He I lines ($5876, 6678, 7065\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) to measure $z^{\pm}$. Jet speed is determined via transverse Doppler effect $\beta = \sqrt{1 - [1 + (z_- + z_+)/2]^{-2}}$, and trajectory perturbations are modeled via power-series expansion $a(\mu) = \sum_k a_k \mu^k$ where $\mu_\pm = \mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{j}^\pm = \pm \sin\theta \cos(\varphi + \psi)$.
papers.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch optical spectroscopic monitoring of the microquasar SS433 to constrain small periodic velocity and directional deviations in its relativistic jets. It establishes a perturbation expansion framework explaining these periodicities via tidal perturbations and dynamical gas stream interactions with the precessing disk.

papers.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
papers.result: No optical counterpart was detected for S251112cm ($d_L = 93 \pm 27\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, chirp mass $\mathcal{M} \in [0.1, 0.87]\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$). Pan-STARRS and Rubin collectively covered $1387\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ (~$80\%$ of the $90\%$ localization region), excluding $\sim 80\%$ of the 3D localization volume for fiducial AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like Type Ic-BL supernova models. If the kilonova is $2\,\mathrm{mag}$ fainter than AT 2017gfo, the joint excluded volume drops to $55\%$, while Rubin alone still excludes $99\%$ within its footprint. The candidate AT 2025alqe is ruled out via VLT/FORS2 spectroscopy yielding $z = 0.09832 \pm 0.00010$ ($D_L \approx 452\,\mathrm{Mpc}$).
papers.problem: Searching for electromagnetic counterparts to the rare sub-solar mass compact binary merger candidate S251112cm ($P(M < 1\,\mathrm{M}_\odot) > 99\%$) to distinguish between progenitor channels such as primordial black holes, collapsar accretion disk fragmentation, and low-mass neutron star mergers.
papers.method: Multi-facility optical follow-up combining Pan-STARRS ($1084\,\mathrm{deg}^2$, $m_{w_\mathrm{ps}} \sim 21.9\,\mathrm{mag}$), ATLAS ($1545\,\mathrm{deg}^2$, $m_o \sim 19.3\,\mathrm{mag}$), and Vera C. Rubin Observatory Target of Opportunity observations ($849\,\mathrm{deg}^2$, $g \sim 24.5\,\mathrm{mag}$, $i \sim 23.5\,\mathrm{mag}$), evaluated against MOSFiT `bns_generative` kilonova and radioactive nickel-powered Type Ic-BL templates with candidate vetting criteria including $|\Delta m / \Delta t| < 0.1\,\mathrm{mag\,d^{-1}}$ rejection and VLT/FORS2 host spectroscopy.
papers.reason: This paper presents coordinated wide-field optical follow-up of the sub-solar mass compact binary merger candidate S251112cm with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, ruling out optical counterparts across ~80% of the localization volume.

papers.title: SN 2017gkk: A moderately luminous and fast evolving Type IIb supernova
papers.result: The event reached a peak absolute magnitude $M_V = -17.01 \pm 0.07\,\mathrm{mag}$ with rise time $t_{\rm rise}(V) = 13.09_{-0.74}^{+0.71}\,\mathrm{days}$ at $D_{\mathrm{L}} = 19.05 \pm 0.59\,\mathrm{Mpc}$. Peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity is $L_{\rm bol} = (8.37 \pm 0.19) \times 10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and black-body bolometric peak is $L_{\rm bol, BB} = (2.15 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ via $L_{\mathrm{Bol,BB}} = 4\pi R_{\mathrm{BB}}^2 \sigma T_{\mathrm{BB}}^4$. Post-peak decline is rapid with $\gamma_{25<t<80}(V) = 2.35 \pm 0.06\,\mathrm{mag\times(100\,days)^{-1}}$. Analytical modeling yields ejecta mass $M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.38_{-0.31}^{+0.48}\,M_\odot$, nickel mass fraction $f_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.055_{-0.012}^{+0.013}$, ejecta velocity $v_{\mathrm{ej}} = 9120_{-410}^{+430}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, and $\gamma$-ray leakage timescale $t_{\rm leak} = 59.57_{-2.02}^{+2.10}\,\mathrm{days}$ (opacity $\kappa_\gamma = 0.033_{-0.010}^{+0.011}\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}$). Late-time line flux ratio $[\mathrm{Ca\ II}]/[\mathrm{O\ I}] = 1.686_{-0.130}^{+0.145}$ and oxygen mass $M_{\mathrm{O}} \approx 0.023\,M_\odot$ from $M_{\mathrm{O}} = 10^8 d_{\mathrm{L}}^2 f([\mathrm{O\,I}]) \times \exp(2.28/T_4)\,M_\odot$ constrain the progenitor zero-age main-sequence mass to $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \approx 12\,M_\odot$.
papers.problem: Investigating the progenitor physical nature, envelope stripping channel (single-star stellar wind vs. binary interaction), explosion energetics, and 56Ni mixing in the fast-evolving Type IIb stripped-envelope core-collapse supernova SN 2017gkk.
papers.method: Optical BVRI photometry and low-resolution spectroscopy reduction with template image subtraction; bolometric light curve synthesis via black-body SED fitting governed by $L_{\mathrm{Bol,BB}} = 4\pi R_{\mathrm{BB}}^2 \sigma T_{\mathrm{BB}}^4$; semi-analytical radioactive decay diffusion modeling of $^{56}\mathrm{Ni} \rightarrow {}^{56}\mathrm{Co}$; and nebular forbidden-line diagnostic modeling calibrated by NLTE radiative transfer models and oxygen mass scaling $M_{\mathrm{O}} = 10^8 d_{\mathrm{L}}^2 f([\mathrm{O\,I}]) \times \exp(2.28/T_4)\,M_\odot$.
papers.reason: SN 2017gkk is a fast-evolving, moderately luminous Type IIb stripped-envelope supernova that provides quantitative observational constraints on core-collapse explosion parameters, 56Ni production, and progenitor envelope stripping mechanisms.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
